BiblicalUsage: Derision is the noun for being laughed to scorn, and it is mostly what God's people suffer at the hands of their enemies. In Psalms 44:13 God has made Israel "a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us," in Job 34:7 Job is accused of drinking up scorning like water, and in Ezekiel 23:32 Jerusalem will drink her sister's cup and be "laughed to scorn and had in derision."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that derision is the lot of God's people in a mocking world, and the psalms give me the words for it: they laughed at Israel, they laughed at Job, and God heard every laugh. The laughter of the proud is the lot of the righteous, and God will answer it.
